description: The plot illustrates how model perplexity and GPU memory ratio vary as the “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” changes, using two y-axes. The x-axis is labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly 10% to 100% with labeled ticks at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. The left y-axis is labeled “Perplexity” on a linear scale from about 4.2 to 4.7 with ticks every 0.1, and it includes a horizontal red dashed reference line labeled “Full Cache PPL” at approximately 4.38. The right y-axis is labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)” on a linear scale from 40% to 100% with ticks every 10%, and it includes a horizontal blue dashed reference line labeled “Full Cache GPU Mem.” at 100%. One line shows perplexity as an orange solid line with circular markers: it starts near 4.59 at 10%, decreases through about 4.45 (20%), ~4.39 (30%), reaching a low around 4.30 at 40%, then rises slightly to ~4.33 (50%) and ~4.34 (60%), dips to ~4.29 at 70%, increases to ~4.33 at 80%, and ends around ~4.39 at 90% and ~4.38 at 100%. The other line shows GPU memory ratio as a blue solid line with circular markers: it begins near 41% at 10%, increases gradually to about 42% (20%), ~43% (30%), ~44% (40%), ~45% (50%), ~46% (60%), and ~48% (70%), then rises to roughly ~55% at 80%, jumps sharply to about ~98% at 90%, and finishes near ~99–100% at 100%.
